headline: FED SPLIT 9-8 AT JULY MEETING — FOMC MINUTES CONFIRM THREE DISSENTERS WANTED HIKE, GOLD HOLDS $4,475 AND BARELY BLINKS
snippet: The July 28-29 FOMC meeting minutes, released August 19 at 2pm ET, confirmed that Chair Warsh held rates at 3.50-3.75% despite three dissents from regional Fed presidents Logan, Hammack, and Kashkari — all pushing for an immediate 25-basis-point hike. Gold recovered 1.9% from Tuesday's $4,390 low to near $4,475 ahead of the release, then barely moved after — a signal markets had largely pre-priced the hawkish split. September rate hike odds remain near 30%, and Warsh's August 28 Jackson Hole keynote is the next defined binary event for gold pricing.

headline: CRITICAL METALS CORP BAGS SECOND US RARE EARTH OFFTAKE FOR TANBREEZ — REALLOYS + UCORE COMMIT 25% OF GREENLAND GIANT'S OUTPUT
snippet: Critical Metals Corp. (NASDAQ:CRML) signed a letter of intent with US-based REalloys for a ten-year offtake covering 15% of production from its 92.5%-owned Tanbreez rare earth project in southern Greenland, following its earlier August deal with Ucore Rare Metals for 10% — bringing total committed supply to 25% before the pilot plant's Stage 1 completion this month. The stock has surged 757% over the past year on successive catalysts: Greenland government approval of the expanded ownership stake, two US-flagged strategic offtakes, and operational camp and drilling infrastructure now in place. At 25% pre-committed without yet reaching resource stage, Tanbreez is setting a new benchmark for de-risking a Western heavy rare earth project outside of China.

headline: AMERICAN EAGLE GOLD DRILLS 1,001 METRES OF COPPER-GOLD FROM SURFACE AT NAK — 218 METRES OF 1.01% CuEq IN BC PORPHYRY STEP-OUT
snippet: American Eagle Gold Corp. (TSXV:AE) announced August 18 that step-out hole NAK26-87 at its NAK Copper-Gold Project in British Columbia returned 1,001 metres grading 0.46% CuEq from surface — including 218 metres of 1.01% CuEq — the longest uninterrupted copper-gold intersection reported at the project to date and a strong indicator of a large-tonnage porphyry system. At $14,500/t copper and $4,400 gold, a system capable of returning 218m of 1% CuEq from 27 metres depth represents the kind of scale that draws project-level attention from mid-tier acquirers in a copper market up 46% year-over-year.

headline: GLADIATOR METALS HITS 40.0m AT 1.98% Cu AND 920 ppm Mo AT COWLEY SKARN — ALL 28 HOLES STRIKE HIGH-GRADE COPPER-MOLYBDENUM
snippet: Gladiator Metals Corp. (TSXV:GLAD) released August 19 results from 28 holes totalling 4,218 metres at its Cowley porphyry-skarn project, with the headline intercept returning 40.0 metres grading 1.98% Cu, 0.31 g/t Au, 13.29 g/t Ag, and 920 ppm molybdenum — a polymetallic assay combination that defines a high-grade copper-molybdenite skarn system. Every hole in the program struck significant high-grade copper-gold-silver-molybdenite skarn, with mineralization extending to the northeast and shallow up-dip to surface, two geometric attributes that are constructive for open-pit economics at a stage when the system remains open in multiple directions.

headline: KARUS MINING HITS SHV GOLD TARGET IN ALL SIX SOUTH CARIBOO HOLES — 2,031 METRES COMPLETE, ASSAYS PENDING AT FG GOLD PROJECT
snippet: Karus Mining Corp. (CSE:KARU) reported August 19 that all three completed and assessed holes from its planned 7,500-metre FG Gold drill program in British Columbia's South Cariboo Gold District intersected the target sediment-hosted vein (SHV) horizon, validating the geological model ahead of first assay results. The program is 27% complete at 2,031 metres across six holes, focused on extending two high-grade vein corridors discovered in 2020/21 that run approximately 650 metres along strike and remain open to the northwest. Hitting the target horizon in every hole is the structural prerequisite for the grade question; assays will answer whether the SHV is economic at Cariboo depths.

headline: STORM EXPLORATION CLEARS DRILL PERMIT AT ONTARIO VMS TARGET — Q3 DRILLING TO TEST GOLD STANDARD PROJECT MASSIVE SULPHIDE
snippet: Storm Exploration Inc. (TSXV:STRM) announced August 19 that it received a drill permit for its Gold Standard Project in northwestern Ontario, clearing the final permitting hurdle before Q3 2026 drilling begins on a Volcanogenic Massive Sulphide (VMS) target. VMS systems in the Superior Province of Ontario have historically hosted high-grade polymetallic gold, silver, copper, and zinc mineralization at relatively shallow depths — a geological setting where first-pass drilling carries above-average discovery probability relative to other deposit types.

headline: BCM RESOURCES DEPLOYS ZONGE INTERNATIONAL IP AND MT SURVEY OVER THOMPSON KNOLLS PORPHYRY-SKARN, UTAH
snippet: BCM Resources Corp. (TSXV:B) announced August 19 that contractor Zonge International has commenced systematic ground-induced polarization (IP) and magnetotellurics (MT) surveys over its 100%-controlled Thompson Knolls porphyry-skarn discovery in Utah, targeting sub-surface copper-gold system geometry ahead of drill program design. The combination of IP chargeability and MT resistivity imaging is the standard pre-drill toolkit for defining porphyry depth extensions where surface mapping alone cannot constrain the bulk tonnage potential.

headline: GOLD CONSOLIDATES UNDER $4,500 AS FED HIKE FEARS SUBSIDE — GOLDEN CROSS AND RENEWED FUND INFLOWS SET UP BREAKOUT CASE
snippet: Gold's Wednesday consolidation at $4,475 — up 1.9% from Tuesday's $4,390 low — is forming a textbook bull-flag structure below $4,500 resistance, with technical analysis flagging a developing golden cross (50-day EMA crossing the 200-day EMA) that reinforces the intermediate-term trend. When hawkish news fails to push gold lower, the path of least resistance shifts higher: fund flows returned after Monday's bond-market rout, and FX Empire identifies $4,500 as the trigger for a move toward the prior record high above $4,600 set in July. Key support: $4,335-4,347.

headline: GLENCORE, ANGLO, RIO TINTO SAY CRITICAL MINERALS M&A SCRUTINY IS MANAGEABLE — NEW NATIONAL SECURITY REVIEWS WON'T BLOCK DEAL WAVE
snippet: Senior executives at Glencore, Anglo American, and Rio Tinto said after their H1 2026 results that national security and antitrust reviews are becoming standard procedure for critical minerals M&A — particularly transactions involving copper, cobalt, and rare earths — but they do not see the shift as a fundamental barrier to dealmaking. The comments follow the formalization of critical minerals review frameworks across the US, EU, Canada, and Australia in the past 24 months. The $50 billion Anglo American-Teck Resources merger remains the sector's highest-profile test case for how these new regulatory regimes interact with large-scale transactions.

headline: GOLDSEEK: GDX COULD REACH NEW HIGHS BY YEAR-END — MINERS TRADING AT LOWEST P/E IN 41 QUARTERS DESPITE RECORD MARGINS
snippet: A fresh GoldSeek analysis argues that the VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) is positioned to reclaim all-time highs before year-end as the market re-rates mining equities toward their fundamental value at $4,400 gold. The author notes that GDX's top-25 miners are generating $2,600+ per-ounce margins at current gold prices yet trade at just 16.5x trailing earnings — the lowest multiple in 41 quarters — while institutional allocations to gold equities remain near decade lows. The historical pattern after gold sustains above a new psychological threshold for multiple quarters is a catch-up phase where miners outperform the metal; GDX's year-to-date underperformance of gold sets up that dynamic for H2 2026.
